narrative.northStar: Clean professional editor with playful block accents
narrative.overview:
PinIt gives customer artwork most of the working area. Cool neutral canvas, white panels and compact Geist typography support repeated positioning and print preparation. Dark blue marks working actions and selected tools; the cyan and sky reference colors remain small identity accents.

Molded studs appear in the cropped brand symbol and one outer canvas corner. This explicitly selected refinement supersedes the rejected broad colored block workbench and its decorative stud density. The implemented source is the authority; this is a code-led refinement with no approved visual comp or new concept seed claimed.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet dotted artwork canvas, white controls and a simultaneous white sheet preview.
Locally bundled Geist, compact task headings and precise numeric fields.
Restrained cyan/sky accents, dark blue active tools and two bounded stud placements.
Shared artwork-tray and dock row, disclosed exact adjustments and persistent tool labels.
Independent print geometry, numeric gesture alternatives and local operational feedback.

rules.name: The Working Color Rule
rules.body: Keep canvas and panels neutral, working actions dark blue, and the reference cyan/sky palette as restrained identity and selection accents.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Use the locally bundled Geist variable face through PinIt Sans for headings, controls and operational text.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep ordinary panels, controls, cards and dock flat; reserve modeled lighting for the bounded studs and cast lift for selected fit, paper and operational overlays.

dos: Do use locally bundled Geist, the implemented neutral palette and restrained cyan/sky accents.
Do preserve the large artwork stage, shared tray/dock row and persistent sheet preview.
Do retain exact numeric controls, meaningful labels, tabular figures and aligned paired fields.
Do pair operational color with text, visible focus, associated validation and recovery controls.
Do preserve independent face/cut dimensions and exclude editing overlays from exports.
Do keep dock labels, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion behavior and fine-pointer gates.
Do keep the molded stud motif in the brand symbol and clipped outer canvas corner.
donts: Don't restore the rejected broad colored block workbench or decorative stud density as preservation requirements.
Don't place decorative blocks over customer artwork or spread molded lighting to ordinary controls.
Don't use customer pixels, review imagery or native-icon colors as UI design tokens.
Don't change physical measurements to fit the viewport or round stored values for visual alignment.
Don't let dock magnification move keyboard controls, run for coarse pointers/reduced motion or cover editing work.
Don't treat the defensive narrow-browser layout as a new native mobile product claim.
Don't reuse 9px source/narrow annotations as general body or control text.
